title: C3212 — RH B-pillar side impact sensor
introduction:
I start this reference with the right-hand B-pillar identity, then let the cavity labels lead me through the circuit table. The component name gives the neighborhood; the cavity map gives the address. Read CNumber and Description first, then match each illustrated label to its Cavity row and follow that row through Circuit Number, Color, Gauge and Function.

Read the sensor and control-module function descriptions literally. A negative mark appears where specified; an unmarked function is not an invitation to invent a positive designation. The pigtail table provides a separate catalog cross-reference, with its own Gauge entry rather than a wire-selection instruction.

This page supports connector identification and reference reading. Access, restraint-system preparation, disconnection, probing and repairs need separate applicable instructions. Physical viewing direction, gauge convention and the Box, Size and Used codes are undefined here. COMPLETE describes the reference record and says nothing about the installed sensor's condition.

edits.why: I locate the rounded rectangular cavity area on the right and the broad rectangular housing section on the left, with shaped projections above and below. Those landmarks keep the upper and lower cavity labels tied to this drawing. They do not establish a physical viewing side or explain how the connector releases.

Following a complete row keeps the passenger-side sensor function attached to its circuit identity and color code. The control-module connection carries the printed negative designation; the other function has no printed positive designation. These labels describe assignments, without establishing a voltage, signal waveform or chassis-ground test.

I use Kit List and Number to connect the identity table to the pigtail listing, then compare Hard Shell and Fpn with Engineering Shell. Service Part is the catalog reference for that listing. The table's material, gauge and cavity fields describe the pigtail without teaching a splice, terminal repair or replacement decision.
